describes: The bounds on how a session works: how many fixes that each failed it makes against one failure before it stops and reports (`rootCauseMaxFixes`, which the `root-cause` and `open-pr` skills read), how many reviews one issue's change gets before its open gaps go to the operator (`reviewMaxRounds`, which the `work` skill and the `fan-out-work` agent read), and how many lanes one sweep dispatches (`fanOutMaxLanes`, which the `fan-out-work` agent reads).
whyThisFileExists: A bound a prompt follows is a constant, and a constant a prompt reads lives in a policy file under a key, with its reason beside it (`AGENTS.md` § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth), so the skill cites the key and spells no number. It is a record of its own, apart from `policy/tool-settings.json`, because it bounds a session rather than a tool.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. No gate holds the value of `rootCauseMaxFixes`, `reviewMaxRounds` or `fanOutMaxLanes`: a session reads each while it works, which no gate sees.
whatItDoesNOTDo: It holds no rule about how a session finds a failure's cause, or what counts as a fix that failed, which `.harness/skills/root-cause/SKILL.md` says. It holds no rule about which gaps earn another review, which `.harness/skills/work/SKILL.md` § 6 says, or about what makes a gap blocking, which `.harness/agents/spec-reviewer.md` says. It holds no rule about how issues are split into lanes, which `.harness/agents/fan-out-work.md` says. It holds only how many such fixes a session makes, how many reviews a change gets and how many lanes a sweep starts.
provenance: Came with the template this repository was bootstrapped from; each key's `Means` gives the reason for its value.
rootCauseMaxFixesMeans: How many fixes that each failed a session makes against one failure before it makes no further fix and reports to the user what it tested, as `.harness/skills/root-cause/SKILL.md` § 6 says, which also says what counts as a fix that failed: a run that fixes past it is guessing, and the design may be what is wrong, which is the user's call. The skill reads it by key and spells no number, and so does `.harness/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md` § 6, which counts each push that left a pull request's check failing as a fix that failed. 3 is the number obra/superpowers' `systematic-debugging` skill uses at 8ca22db, which nothing in this repository has measured. Where it loses: a failure with several independent causes, each fix right but partial, stops at the third fix and waits on a person, although the run was converging.
reviewMaxRoundsMeans: How many reviews the `spec-reviewer` agent makes of one issue's change, the first included, before the session makes no further fix and gives the operator each blocking gap still open, as `.harness/skills/work/SKILL.md` § 6 says. That section also says which gaps earn another review: a blocking gap in the issue's scope does, and a minor one is fixed with no review of its own. A change still blocked after that many reviews is not converging, and its design or its scope may be what is wrong, which is the operator's call. The skill reads it by key and spells no number, and so does `.harness/agents/fan-out-work.md` § 6, which counts each issue of a sweep against it on its own. 3 is a first review and two re-reviews; it matches `rootCauseMaxFixes`, and nothing in this repository has measured it. Where it loses: a large change whose third review finds one last real defect that is cheap to fix waits on a person, where a fourth review would have closed it.
fanOutMaxLanesMeans: How many lanes the `fan-out-work` agent dispatches in one sweep (`.harness/agents/fan-out-work.md` § 2); the ready issues past it wait for the next sweep. Each lane is a session in its own worktree that runs the gates, so the sweep's spend, and the reports the dispatcher reads back, grow with every lane, and an unbounded sweep is a loop with no cap. The agent reads it by key and spells no number. 4 is a starting figure that nothing in this repository has measured. Where it loses: a queue of many small, disjoint issues takes several sweeps where one could have taken it.
